quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do before you move your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children can hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not depend only on your mirrors, especially when children are near. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing out of a driveway.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Let any vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you generally do?

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. When merging, signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge smoothly.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a suggested driving speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed when road and weather are good.
The maximum safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed when road and weather are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit shows the maximum legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: Your stopping distance increases in which condition?

options.text: On wet or icy roads.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On wet or icy roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do after one train passes?

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing.
Look for another train on the other track before going.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for another train on the other track before going.
questions.explanation: With two tracks side by side, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: What are highway signs called when they require drivers to obey an instruction?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking the rules on these signs can result in a penalty.

questions.question: What colors are used on signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters.
Black with white letters.
Red with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters.
questions.explanation: Signs that show destinations and directions are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Mean your vehicle needs a tune-up sooner.
Make you feel sleepy while driving.
Start fires in grass on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases and cools hot gases from your engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system are toxic and dangerous. They can make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for one hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat causes more oil to rise to the surface.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Go ahead because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means stop. Come to a complete stop and go only when it is safe. A stop sign may also be posted at this location.

questions.question: The minimum and maximum speed limits on Missouri interstate highways are:

options.text: 40 mph and 55 mph.
40 mph and 70 mph.
30 mph and 70 mph.
55 mph and 75 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 mph and 70 mph.
questions.explanation: On Missouri interstate highways, the highest speed limit is 70 mph. The lowest speed limit is 40 mph under normal road conditions.

questions.question: What is the youngest age to get an instruction permit?

options.text: 14 years old.
15 years old.
15 and one-half years old.
16 years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 years old.
questions.explanation: You can get an instruction permit at age 15. This permit lets you practice driving with a licensed adult.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Go when the car ahead of you goes.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers let you through.
Drive around a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Stopping completely at an intersection, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians, then going when it is safe describes:

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: The most important thing about managing speed on curves is:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit entering the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Speed up gently before entering the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Your car's momentum makes turning harder. Slow down before you enter a curve to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn before you shift into reverse.
Look behind the vehicle before you sit down in the driver's seat.
Look in your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio to get the attention of people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look behind the vehicle before you sit down in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Before you get in the car, walk to the back and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you look?

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: When a car with Anti-Lock Brakes loses grip on a slippery road, what should the driver do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Tap the brakes lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle loses grip on a slippery road, press the brake pedal hard, keep holding it, and steer to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will pump the brakes for you faster than you can. If you pump the brakes or reduce pressure, the ABS will not work.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed on a road under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones and work zones. If bad weather or road work makes the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.
